pages.title: Real-time WebRTC collaboration
pages.description: Multi-cursor editing over a peer-to-peer mesh — no server account, no central log of your doc.
pages.md:
Lumen ships a real-time collab mode powered by [Yjs](https://yjs.dev)
over WebRTC. Open a doc, share the room link, and every keystroke
syncs to every peer in <30 ms.

## Start a session

`⌘K → Start collaboration`. A toast confirms the room name + copies
the share link to your clipboard:

```
https://lumen.app/#room=lumen-bright-river-77
```

Anyone with the link enters the same Y.Doc. Their cursor + selection
appears in your editor, coloured by their auto-assigned chip.

## Awareness UI

Each peer publishes:

- **Display name** — random adjective+noun combo, e.g. "Marble".
- **Colour** — auto-picked HSL hue.
- **Cursor + selection** — re-published on every selection change.

The editor renders peer cursors with a small floating name tag above
the caret. A peer's selection highlights with a translucent version of
their colour. The list of active peers shows in the status bar.

## End-to-end encryption

Without a password, the room is **not** end-to-end encrypted. Peers sync
the plaintext Yjs document, so any signaling server that relays
messages, the persistent collab server and anyone with the room link can
read it.

Set `localStorage["lumen.collab.password"]` (or append `&password=…` to
the share link) to change that. The editor's document then stays
local, and only AES-GCM-256 ciphertext envelopes (key = PBKDF2 of the
password, salted with the room name) go to the mesh and to any
persistence server. Peers without the password receive only ciphertext
and see a "Can't decrypt this room" error.

The password also encrypts y-webrtc's signaling, so a peer without it
can't connect at all and relays never see presence (names, colours,
cursor positions) — only peers holding the password do. Metadata such
as the room name and the volume and timing of edits is still visible.
A wrong password therefore looks like an empty room: Lumen asks before
sharing your document into it rather than forking the room silently. See
[End-to-end encryption](/collab/encryption/) for the full threat model.

## Rooms evaporate when the last peer leaves

WebRTC is peer-to-peer — there's no server holding the doc. The doc
state lives in each peer's Y.Doc, replicated over the mesh. Once
everyone leaves, the state is only in the OPFS workspace of whoever
saved it. To get persistent rooms (the Notion / Google Docs feel),
enable [persistent collab](/collab/persistent/).

## Comments / annotations

Inline comments anchor to text ranges via Yjs `RelativePosition`, so a
comment on "neural networks" stays attached to those words even when
collaborators insert paragraphs above. Open the comments panel from
`⌘K → View comments panel`.

## Performance budget

- Room cap: 20 simultaneous peers (raise via the WebRTC provider's
  `maxConns`).
- Per-update overhead in password rooms: ≈ 40 bytes (IV + GCM tag +
  envelope framing) per edit batch; edits made in the same tick share
  one envelope.
- Initial join: full Y.Doc snapshot synced via the signaling channel
  (≈ 1 KB per 1k characters of doc).

For documents larger than ~50k characters or sessions with >20 peers,
move to [persistent collab](/collab/persistent/) which uses
the persistent collab server (Hocuspocus + SQLite, `sync-server/collab-server.mjs`).

pages.title: Budgets that only go down
pages.description: The bundle budgets and the performance gate's FCP and LCP limits are lowered after every train to what the train measured plus 2 %, and never raised. Exceptions carry an expiry date and fail once it has passed.
pages.md:
Lumen's size and speed limits only move one way: down (plan W6.26).
A budget that stays put after a saving invites the next growth.

## Where the limits live

| File | What it limits | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/bundle-budgets.json` | Each chunk class (KB gzipped, per file) and the startup total | `npm run budget` |
| `perf-gate.config.json` | FCP and LCP of each profile, and the other metrics | `npm run perf:gate` |
| `lighthouserc.json` | Lighthouse scores and metrics | `npm run lighthouse` |

The first rule in `bundle-budgets.json` whose pattern matches a file
name sets that file's budget, so narrower patterns come first.

## After each train: the ratchet

The train's Vercel build runs the budget gate, which writes the
receipt `reports/bundle-sizes.json` and prints it as one
`bundle-sizes: {…}` line in the build log. Feed either one to the ratchet:

```bash
npm run budget:ratchet -- --sizes reports/bundle-sizes.json --train train-3 --sha <head>
npm run budget:ratchet -- --sizes-log vercel-build.log --perf perf-gate.json --first-party startup.log --write
```

- Each budget becomes the biggest measured file of its class plus 2 %
  (at least 1 KB), rounded up to a whole KB, but only when that is
  lower than the budget today. The startup total works the same way.
- With `--perf` (the JSON of `npm run perf:gate -- --json`), the FCP
  and LCP limits (`error` and `warn`) become the median run plus 2 %
  (at least 50 ms), when that is lower. Targets don't change.
- `--first-party` takes the log of the offline startup measure
  (`startup first-party: … KB gz`) and records it in the history,
  since the Vite build can't tell our own code from package code.
- Without `--write` it only prints what would go down. With `--write`
  it updates the files and appends a line to `history` in
  `bundle-budgets.json`. Commit that as its own commit.

## Exceptions expire

A rule with `expires` (YYYY-MM-DD) is an exception, and it must also
name the `task` that removes it. Today there is one: the Excalidraw
core module at 740 KB, until 2027-01-15, removed by W1.36. From the day
after its date, `npm run budget` fails until the rule is lowered or
decided again with a new date, and pr:check fails a later date.
To check a build on another day, set `LUMEN_TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD`.

## No raise gets in

- `npm run pr:check` fails a diff that loosens any of the three files.
  It compares the budget each chunk name gets before and after, so a
  raised number, a new rule wider than the one its files fell under, a
  removed rule whose files fall to a bigger one and a reordering all
  count. So do a later or dropped expiry date, a wider margin, a
  performance limit raised, removed or turned from `error` into `warn`,
  fewer runs, and a lower Lighthouse level or score. A budget number
  written into `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs` itself fails too.
- `npm run budget:history` checks every commit of the three files since
  the ratchet began and names any commit that raised a limit. Pass
  `-- --since all` to see the whole history, including the decisions
  made before the ratchet.

When a budget fails, split the chunk or load it lazily. The budget
doesn't move up.

pages.title: Checks on every branch (Vercel)
pages.description: Lumen's gates run in the Vercel build of every branch, without GitHub Actions — what runs, what a red status means, and where the old CI checks went.
pages.md:
`main` and the integration trains (`verify/…`) get a Vercel build when
pushed, and Vercel reports it on the commit as the **Vercel** status; a pull
request's own branch is verified through the train (see
[Builds that are skipped](#builds-that-are-skipped)). That build is Lumen's gate: the build
command is `node scripts/vercel-build.mjs` (in `deploy/vercel.base.json`),
and a preview build runs every check. A pull request with a failing test or
a broken gate gets a red **Vercel** status; a clean one gets a green one.
No GitHub Actions minutes are used.

| Build | What runs, in order |
|---|---|
| Preview (the `verify/…` trains) | build, bundle budget, the secret scan of `dist/`, vitest, e2e (smoke on chromium and firefox), `i18n:check`, hygiene, `docs:sync`, the licence gate |
| Production (`main`) | build, bundle budget — as before |

The gates stop at the first failure. The build log ends with the gate that
failed and the ones that passed before it, with their times:

```text
✗ vercel-build: the vitest gate failed (212.4 s, exit 1). Passed before it: build 95.1 s, budget 1.2 s.
```

## Builds that are skipped

Vercel builds one deployment at a time, so every queued build delays the
ones behind it. `scripts/vercel-ignore.sh` (the config's `ignoreCommand`)
skips a build before it starts when:

- its branch is neither `main` (production) nor an integration train
  (`verify/…`): a pull request's branch is verified through the train
  (`verify/train-2`), so it does not build on its own. Setting the Vercel
  project variable `LUMEN_BUILD_ALL=1` builds every branch again;
- its commit is no longer the head of its branch: a newer push is queued
  and will be built instead. When the branch head cannot be read (no
  network, a deleted branch), the next rule decides;
- the commit changes nothing the web build reads (Markdown outside `src/`
  and `public/`, the docs site, the other deployables).

A skipped build shows as **Canceled** in Vercel, not as a pass: the
branch's status comes from its newest commit.

## Running the same checks locally

```bash
node scripts/vercel-build.mjs              # the preview set
node scripts/vercel-build.mjs --production # build and budget only
node scripts/vercel-build.mjs --dry-run    # print the gates, run nothing
```

Outside Vercel (no `VERCEL_ENV`) the script runs the preview set, so a
local run is what the branch's build will do. Each gate is also an npm
script of its own: `npm run build`, `npm run budget`, `npm test`,
`npm run e2e:gate` (after `VITE_E2E=1 npm run build`: specs reach the app's modules through `window.__lumenTest`, which only such a build has), `npm run i18n:check`, `npm run hygiene`, `npm run docs:sync`,
`npm run licenses`, `npm run secrets:dist` (see
[Secret scan of the build](/security/secret-scan/)).

## What does not run in the build

Checks that need browsers, devices or signing keys can't run in a Vercel
build. They run in a Vercel Sandbox (W1.1) or on a developer machine:

| Plan task | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| 8.3 Lighthouse gate | an LHCI job on every PR | `npm run lighthouse` (median of 5 runs, the thresholds in `lighthouserc.json`) in the Sandbox, against the preview's build; not a build step, since it needs Chromium |
| 0.19 PR gate (Danger.js, size-limit) | a Danger comment and size-limit on every PR | the size part is the **bundle budget** gate (every main chunk has a budget, `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs`); an unlisted network call fails **vitest** (`src/__tests__/cloudRoutes.test.ts` audits every cloud route); the licence diff is the **licence gate**. The PR comment itself has no replacement yet |
| 13.3 Android and iOS builds | mobile builds in CI | `npm run android:sync` / `npm run ios:sync` on a machine with the SDKs (iOS needs macOS); the web part they ship is what the preview build checks |
| 13.4 Release pipeline | a release workflow | a local release script, signed artifacts and rollback on a developer machine; the web app's release is the production build |
| Playwright e2e | e2e jobs on every PR | the **e2e** gate runs `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` on chromium and firefox in the build (`scripts/e2e-gate.mjs`); the whole suite runs with `npx playwright test` on a developer machine or in the Sandbox (W1.1), since on the build machine the chromium project alone takes about 30 minutes. WebKit cannot run in the build: Playwright's WebKit needs glibc 2.38 and the build image (Amazon Linux 2023) has 2.34. Safari is covered on a Mac (W4.22) |

## When a gate is red

Open the Vercel deployment from the commit's status and read the end of
the build log: the failing gate is named there. Fix it on the branch and
push again; Vercel builds the new commit. A failing gate is never skipped
or loosened to get a green status.

pages.title: Design system
pages.description: Lumen's tokens for colour, space, radius, type, elevation and motion, the rules the code is held to, and the shared components.
pages.md:
Every surface of Lumen draws from one set of tokens. They are CSS custom
properties in `src/index.css`, so dark mode, the theme presets (Settings →
Theme) and *reduce motion* change them in one place. Inline styles use them
through `src/ui/tokens.ts`.

## Tokens

| Group | Tokens | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Surfaces and text | `--bg`, `--bg-subtle`, `--bg-muted`, `--bg-inset`, `--fg`, `--fg-subtle`, `--fg-muted`, `--border`, `--border-strong`, `--accent`, `--accent-fg` | HSL triplets: `hsl(var(--bg))`, `hsl(var(--accent) / 0.15)` |
| Status | `--danger`, `--success`, `--warning`, `--info` | errors and destructive actions, confirmations, cautions, information; tuned for light and dark |
| Gradients | `--gradient-brand`, `--gradient-ai`, `--gradient-success` | the logo, the AI button, progress — decoration only |
| Behind a modal | `--overlay` | every dialog backdrop |
| Elevation | `--shadow-sm`, `--shadow-md`, `--shadow-lg`, `--shadow-xl`, `--shadow-accent` | badges, popovers, menus, dialogs; the accent glow |
| Space | `--space-1` … `--space-8` (4 px steps) | padding and gaps |
| Radius | `--radius-sm` 4, `--radius-md` 6, `--radius-lg` 10, `--radius-full` | |
| Type | `--text-xs` 11 … `--text-xl` 18 px | |
| Motion | `--duration-fast` 100 ms, `--duration-base` 250 ms, `--duration-slow` 350 ms; `--ease-out`, `--ease-in-out` | menus and hovers; dialogs and toasts; panels |

In TypeScript: `color.danger`, `color.tint("danger", 0.1)`, `shadow.lg`,
`transition(["opacity"], "base")`, `enter("cmdSlideIn")`. A `<canvas>`
cannot read `var()`: use `resolvedColor("fg", 0.15)` when drawing.

## Rules

1. **No hard-coded colour in `src/ui`** — no hex, `rgb()` or `hsl()` with
   numbers. Colours a person picks for their content (the note colours of
   the canvas) are content, marked `design-allow`.
2. **Only `transform` and `opacity` move**, with the three durations.
   Nothing animates width, height, top/left or margins: a progress bar
   scales (`transform: scaleX()`), a menu slides (`translateY`), a hover
   changes colour instantly.
3. **Reduce motion is respected everywhere**: with the system setting on,
   the duration tokens become 0 and a global rule cuts every remaining
   animation.
4. **Logical sides**: `marginInlineStart`, `insetInlineEnd`, `textAlign:
   "start"` — a surface mirrors in Hebrew by itself. Viewport coordinates
   from `getBoundingClientRect()` stay physical.
5. **A modal backdrop is `var(--overlay)`; a shadow is a step of the scale.**

`npm run design:check` runs both gates: `scripts/check-design.mjs` (rules
1–2 on all of `src/ui`, and no layout animation anywhere in `src`) and
`scripts/design-audit.mjs`, which runs the checklist (rules 1, 2, 4, 5) on
the 40 surfaces listed in `scripts/design-surfaces.json`. A real exception is
marked `design-allow: <reason>` in the code.

## Shared components

| Component | Where | For |
|---|---|---|
| Dialogs | `uiAlert`, `uiConfirm`, `uiPrompt`, `uiSelect` (`src/ui/PromptDialog.tsx`) | every question and confirmation; never `window.confirm` |
| Modal frame | `.cmd-palette-backdrop` + `.cmd-palette` (`src/ui/CommandPalette.css`) | panels such as the trash, the AI doctor, settings |
| Toasts | `showAiToast()` (`src/ui/AiToast.tsx`), `toast.*` (`src/store/useToastStore.ts`) | short messages; `action` for an Undo |
| Icon button | `.icon-btn` (`src/index.css`) | toolbar and panel buttons |
| Command palette | `src/ui/CommandPalette.tsx` | every action has a command |

pages.title: Nightly runs and receipts
pages.description: npm run nightly runs the flake hunt, the perf checks, the review triage and the weekly health on your own machine, and writes a signed report for each, without GitHub Actions.
pages.md:
Lumen doesn't use GitHub Actions, so the scheduled runs (plan 0.11) and the
measurements that depend on them (0.5: three nights with no flaky test; 0.14:
how many preview-build failures a local `ci:local` run would have caught) run
on the owner's machine. One command does it:

```bash
npm run nightly                  # what is due today
npm run nightly -- --dry-run     # print the plan, run nothing
```

| Kind | When | What runs |
|---|---|---|
| `flake` | every night | `npm run e2e:flake -- --all --times 5` (chromium, firefox, webkit, 5 runs each, no retries) |
| `perf` | every night | build, bundle budget, the `@nightly` perf project, Lighthouse when it is installed |
| `triage` | every night | review triage of the open PRs, and the 0.14 count over the first 20 PRs since 12.11.2026 |
| `weekly` | Sundays (UTC) | dependency health (audit, outdated, licences), and mutation scores when `test:mutation` is there |

`--only flake,perf` picks kinds. The scheduler passes `--scheduled`, which
marks the reports as scheduled. Plan 0.11 counts only those.

## Reports and receipts

Each kind writes `reports/nightly/<date>-<kind>.json`. The report records:

- the commit, and whether the tree was clean
- the machine: platform, Node and CPU count, no host name
- every command with its exit code and duration
- the sha256 of each command's output, with its last lines
- the kind's numbers: flaky and always-failing tests per browser, perf
  annotations, review totals, audit counts

The report is **sealed**. It carries its sha256 and an Ed25519 signature
made with a key that never leaves the machine
(`~/.config/lumen-md/nightly-ed25519.pem`, mode 0600, created on the first
run; `LUMEN_NIGHTLY_KEY` overrides the path). The public half is committed as
`reports/nightly/PUBLIC_KEY.pem`. Anyone can check a committed report:

```bash
npm run nightly -- --verify reports/nightly/2026-11-13-flake.json
```

If any number in the report changed after the run, both the digest and the
signature fail.

`reports/nightly/status.json` (sealed too) is recomputed after every run
(`npm run nightly -- --status` does only that). It records:

- **0.5**: how many consecutive nights each had every browser 5 times, with
  no flaky and no always-failing test (3 are needed)
- **0.11**: which of the four kinds produced a scheduled report (all 4 are
  needed)
- **0.14**: in the first 20 PRs opened since 12.11.2026, the commits whose
  **Vercel** preview build failed. The preview build runs a subset of
  `ci:local`, so each such failure is one `ci:local` would have caught,
  except `docs:sync`, which `ci:local` doesn't run. `verify/*` integration
  branches aren't counted.

`--commit` commits `reports/nightly/` with a `[skip ci]` message. It never
pushes. A commit that changes only `reports/` doesn't start a Vercel build
(`scripts/vercel-ignore.sh`), so receipts don't use up the deployment quota.

## Scheduling it on a Mac (launchd)

Use a clone that is used only for the nightly, on its own branch, so a run
never mixes with your work:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/talstilkol/lumen-md ~/lumen-nightly
cd ~/lumen-nightly && git switch -c nightly/receipts && npm ci && npx playwright install
```

Save `~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.lumen-md.nightly.plist`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key><string>dev.lumen-md.nightly</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/bin/zsh</string><string>-lc</string>
    <string>cd ~/lumen-nightly && git pull -q --rebase origin main && npm ci --silent && npm run nightly -- --scheduled --commit</string>
  </array>
  <key>StartCalendarInterval</key><dict><key>Hour</key><integer>2</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>17</integer></dict>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key><string>/tmp/lumen-nightly.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key><string>/tmp/lumen-nightly.log</string>
</dict>
</plist>
```

Then load it with `launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.lumen-md.nightly.plist`.
launchd runs a job that was missed while the Mac slept as soon as it wakes.
To publish the receipts, push the branch (`git push origin nightly/receipts`)
or open a PR from it. Linux uses cron instead:

```text
17 2 * * *  cd ~/lumen-nightly && git pull -q --rebase origin main && npm ci --silent && npm run nightly -- --scheduled --commit
```

## Why not Vercel Cron or a cloud scheduled task

- **Vercel Cron** only calls a function of a deployment on a schedule. It
  can't run three browsers five times over the e2e suite, and it would spend
  the shared deployment quota.
- **A Claude Code scheduled task** starts a fresh cloud session. That session
  has no browsers and can't install packages, so it can run only the
  `triage` kind (GitHub's REST API) and read the committed receipts. That is
  useful for a morning summary, not for the measurements themselves.

pages.title: The PR check
pages.description: npm run pr:check is the local PR gate that replaces Danger.js and size-limit. It reports bundle size against the base, PR body sections, [skip ci] commits, unregistered network calls, licences and the domain rule.
pages.md:
Lumen runs no GitHub Actions on pull requests. Danger.js and size-limit
need Actions, so one local command replaces them (plan 0.19):

```bash
npm run build
npm run pr:check -- --base origin/main --body pr-body.md --build-base --out pr-check.md
```

The report is Markdown. Paste it into the pull request. The command exits
with 1 when a check fails. Warnings do not fail it.

## The checks

- **Bundle size.** The gzipped size of each chunk class (`npm run budget -- --json`),
  compared with the base, as a table. The bundle budget's own verdict
  decides pass or fail. The base's sizes come from one of:
  - `--base-sizes <file>`;
  - `--build-base`, which builds the merge base in a temporary worktree
    that links this checkout's `node_modules`.
- **Commits.** Every subject from the merge base to `HEAD` contains
  `[skip ci]`.
- **PR body.** The file passed with `--body` has every section, none
  empty:
  - What and why
  - Definition of done (plan 0.7)
  - Local verification
  - Not verified here
  - Owner commands
- **Network.** Every new call that sends a request (`fetch`, `WebSocket`,
  `EventSource`, `sendBeacon`, `importScripts`) goes to a host listed in
  the privacy ledger (`src/ai/privacyLedger.ts`). A call whose URL is
  computed instead needs a `// privacy-ledger: <rule>` comment.
- **Licences.** Every production package added or changed in the
  lockfile has an allowed licence (no copyleft, no non-commercial, not
  missing).
- **Domain.** No added line names the project's domain.
- **Budgets only go down** (plan W6.26). A diff that raises a bundle
  budget, the startup budget, an exception's expiry date, the ratchet
  margin, a performance-gate FCP/LCP limit or a Lighthouse assertion
  fails. So does a budget number written into `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs`
  itself. See [Budgets that only go down](/contributing/budgets/).

It also warns:
- when source changed and no test did;
- when an AI agent wrote the PR (add the `ai-written` label).

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--base <ref>` | The branch the PR goes into (default `origin/main`) |
| `--body <file>` | The PR description, to check its sections |
| `--base-sizes <file>`, `--head-sizes <file>` | Sizes already measured |
| `--build-base` | Build the base to measure it |
| `--no-size` | Skip the size check |
| `--out <file>` | Write the report |

pages.title: Skipped tests
pages.description: Every skipped test says why, for which task and until when; npm run hygiene fails on one that does not, and npm run skips lists them all.
pages.md:
A skipped test looks like coverage but checks nothing. So every call that
skips or defers a test — `test.skip`, `it.skip`, `describe.skip`,
`*.skipIf`, `*.runIf`, `*.fixme`, `*.todo`, in `src/` (Vitest) and `e2e/`
(Playwright) — carries one structured comment, on its line or right above:

```ts
// skip-reason: <why it cannot run here> | task: <plan id or #PR> | until: YYYY-MM-DD
test.skip(dev, "the service worker runs on the production build only");
```

`npm run hygiene` (and so the Vercel preview build) fails when:

- a skip has no `skip-reason`, or it lacks the task or the date;
- the date has passed (fix the test, or justify it again with a new date) or
  is more than a year away;
- `e2e/` holds more than 15 skip calls.

## An engine gap goes through one helper

Playwright's WebKit on Linux has no Origin Private File System, so the vault
tests cannot run there. They call `vaultOrSkip(written, browserName)` from
`e2e/_opfs.ts` after seeding the vault: it skips on WebKit only, and **fails**
on Chromium and Firefox, where a vault that cannot be written is a bug — until
plan W4.12 those tests skipped quietly on every engine.

## The report

`npm run skips` prints every skip with its reason, task and date, sorted by
what it leaves out:

| Kind | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| engine | the flow runs on the other engines |
| setup | the flow runs only in a special setup (production build, dev server, a model or service on the machine, an opt-in measurement) |
| deferred | a `todo`: written down, checks nothing yet |

It ends with the list of vault flows WebKit does not run. `npm run skips --
--json` gives the same as JSON.

pages.title: Translation drafts
pages.description: npm run i18n:draft drafts new UI strings in all seven languages with a local model; drafts stay "needs review" until a person approves them.
pages.md:
Lumen's interface is in eight languages. When you add an English string,
the seven others (Hebrew, Arabic, German, French, Japanese, Russian,
Simplified Chinese) need it too. Instead of leaving them empty, draft them:

```sh
npm run i18n:draft
```

The command finds every English key a language doesn't have yet, drafts it
with a model **on your machine** (Ollama), writes the drafts into
`src/i18n/locales/<lang>/<domain>.json`, and lists each one in
`i18n/needs-review/<domain>.json`. Ten new keys give seventy drafts in one
run.

## Options

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--keys=a.b,c.d` | Draft only these keys |
| `--lang=he,ar` | Only these languages |
| `--model=qwen2.5:7b` | The Ollama model (`OLLAMA_HOST` sets the address, default `http://127.0.0.1:11434`) |
| `--engine=fake` | No model: writes `[he] English text` — a dry run |
| `--list` | What still needs review, per language |
| `--approve=he [--keys=…]` | Mark the Hebrew drafts (or only those keys) as reviewed |

Pass options after `--`: `npm run i18n:draft -- --keys=toolbar.save`.

## What is checked

- Every `{placeholder}` and `` `inline code` `` is swapped for a token the
  model must keep. A draft that loses, repeats or invents one is **not
  written** and is reported.
- A language that already has the key is left alone; re-running drafts
  nothing twice.

## Review

The app shows a draft right away, but the values gate
(`src/__tests__/i18nValues.test.ts`) counts every listed draft as
**untranslated**: Hebrew allows none, the other languages up to 5 %. Read
the drafts, fix what needs fixing in the locale file, then approve:

```sh
npm run i18n:draft -- --approve=he
```

Each entry in `needs-review` keeps a hash of the English text it was drafted
from, so you can tell a draft whose English changed since.

## Engines

Ollama is the engine today. The on-device translation of plan 6.4 (Chrome's
Translator, Opus-MT, M2M100) runs in the browser; it plugs in as another
engine through the same `translate(texts, lang)` interface
(`scripts/lib/i18n-draft.mjs`).

pages.title: Languages in beta, and how to help
pages.description: Six of Lumen's languages were translated by machine and are marked beta until a native speaker reviews them; suggest a better translation from inside the app.
pages.md:
Lumen's interface is in eight languages. **English** is the source and **Hebrew** is
written by native speakers. The other six were translated by machine (plan 9.1) and no
native speaker has reviewed them yet, so Lumen marks them **beta**:

| Language | Status |
|---|---|
| English | source |
| עברית (Hebrew) | native |
| العربية (Arabic) | beta |
| Русский (Russian) | beta |
| Français (French) | beta |
| Deutsch (German) | beta |
| 日本語 (Japanese) | beta |
| 简体中文 (Simplified Chinese) | beta |

In **Settings → General → Language** and in the command palette, a beta language reads
"Русский (бета)", "Français (bêta)" and so on, in the language you are using. When the
interface is in a beta language, Settings says the translation is waiting for a native
speaker's review and links to the suggestion form.

## Suggest a better translation

Command palette → **Suggest a better translation** (also linked under the language setting).

1. Type the words you saw on screen. Lumen finds the strings that contain them, in your
   language or in English.
2. Pick the string and write it the way a native speaker would. Keep every `{placeholder}`
   as it is.
3. **Open on GitHub** opens the project's new-issue form in a new tab, with the title
   (`[i18n:ru] toolbar.save`), the labels `i18n` and `locale:ru`, the English source, the
   current translation and yours. You post it with your own GitHub account. **Copy the
   text** gives you the same text to send any other way.

Nothing is sent from Lumen itself: there is no server and no account in the app. The issue
exists only once you post it.

## Review a whole language

If you are a native speaker and want to review a whole language, the strings are in
`src/i18n/locales/<lang>/*.json`, one file per area. Open a pull request with your fixes.
New strings drafted by a model are listed in `i18n/needs-review/` until a person approves
them ([Translation drafts](/contributing/translation-drafts/)). When a language has been
reviewed, its status in `src/i18n/review.ts` changes from `beta` to `reviewed`, and the beta
mark goes away.

Arabic is Israel's second right-to-left language, so its review also covers the RTL checks
(the RTL matrix, plan 9.5, runs in Arabic too).

pages.title: Visual regression
pages.description: npm run test:visual compares ten surfaces in English and Hebrew, light and dark, with their pixel baselines — locally, no CI needed.
pages.md:
`npm run test:visual` takes 40 screenshots — ten surfaces, in English (LTR)
and Hebrew (RTL), in the light and the dark theme — and compares each with
its baseline. A pixel change nobody meant fails the run; so does a surface
without a baseline.

| Surfaces |
| --- |
| split · source · preview · WYSIWYG · command palette · keyboard shortcuts · plugin gallery · template gallery · theme settings · AI settings |

## First run on a machine

```bash
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:visual:update      # builds, serves dist/, writes visual/__baselines__/<platform>/
```

Open every PNG, then commit the folder. From then on:

```bash
npm run test:visual
```

A failure leaves the expected, actual and diff images in `visual-results/`
(`visual-results/report/index.html`).

## What keeps the shots stable

- The production build, served by `vite preview`.
- Chromium only, 1280×800 at 1×, browser locale en-US and time zone UTC.
- A fixed note (in English or in Hebrew), a fixed clock, no service worker.
- The app's own fonts; animations, transitions, scrollbars and the caret off.
- The parts that depend on the machine (whether a local model runs) are
  masked.

Baselines are per platform: compare on the same kind of machine that wrote
them. Each shot also fails if the page is wider than the viewport — the
commonest RTL layout bug.

## An intended change

pages.md:
This statement covers the Lumen app (web, desktop and mobile builds) at
version **0.1.0**. It was last reviewed on **10 November 2026** and is
updated with every release: a test (`a11yStatement.test.ts`) fails the
build when the version here and the app's version differ.

## Standard

Israel's Equal Rights for Persons with Disabilities regulations (service
accessibility adjustments, regulation 35) require **Israeli Standard
5568**, which adopts **WCAG 2.0 level AA**. Lumen aims for **WCAG 2.2
level AA**, which includes everything WCAG 2.0 AA asks for.

## What is accessible

- **Keyboard:** every feature is a command in the palette (⌘K / Ctrl+K).
  Dialogs keep focus, Escape closes them, and focus returns to where it was.
- **Screen readers:** dialogs, the editor, the palette and the sidebar edge
  have names and roles. The editor speaks the structure of the line the
  cursor lands on (heading and level, task and its state, code block,
  quote), new suggestions, and the start and end of long AI work. It speaks
  in the interface language, Hebrew or English. **Announce cursor position**
  gives the line, the column and the heading above. **Screen reader
  announcements** switches between headings and structure (default), every
  line, and off.
- **Right-to-left:** Hebrew lines read right to left and English lines left
  to right, in the same document.
- **Contrast:** text is at least 4.5:1 in light and dark mode.
- **Zoom and reflow:** at 200 % and 400 % zoom the main screen, the side
  panels and the dialogs fit the window without scrolling sideways. Code
  blocks scroll inside their own box.
- **High contrast:** in Windows high-contrast mode (forced colours), focus,
  buttons and selected items use the system colours.
- **Reduced motion:** with the system setting on, animations and smooth
  scrolling stop.

## How it is checked

- axe-core (WCAG 2.0/2.1 A and AA) on six surfaces, in Hebrew and English,
  in light and dark mode (`e2e/a11y.spec.ts`).
- Reflow at 320 px and 640 px wide on ten surfaces, plus a forced-colours
  focus check (`e2e/reflow.spec.ts`).
- Spoken announcements (`e2e/sr-announce.spec.ts`).
- A fixed journey in Hebrew with NVDA, VoiceOver (macOS and iOS) and
  TalkBack: the [screen reader protocol](/editor/screen-reader-protocol/).

## Known gaps

The [accessibility conformance report](/editor/acr/) lists every WCAG 2.2
level A and AA criterion with its status, and a remediation plan for each
one that is only partly met. In short:

- The screen-reader journey has not yet been run with all three screen
  readers for this version. The results are recorded in the protocol when
  it is.
- Charts, diagrams (Mermaid, Graphviz), the canvas and the map are
  pictures. Their source text in the note is the accessible version.
- Content you write yourself, such as images without alt text, is yours to
  make accessible. The alt-text helper can suggest descriptions.

## Report a barrier

Use the [accessibility report form](https://github.com/talstilkol/lumen-md/issues/new?template=accessibility.yml)
(it is labelled **accessibility**), or **Report an accessibility problem**
in the command palette. Say what you were doing, which screen reader or
tool you used, and what happened. You can write in Hebrew or English.
Accessibility reports are triaged before other bugs.

pages.md:
Lumen is meant to be used without a mouse, with a screen reader, in Hebrew
or English, in light or dark mode.

## Keyboard

- **⌘K / Ctrl+K** opens the command palette; every feature is a command
  there. **⌘/ / Ctrl+/** lists the shortcuts.
- **Dialogs keep focus.** When a dialog opens, focus moves into it. Tab
  and Shift+Tab stay inside it, **Escape** closes it, and focus returns to
  where it was before (for example the editor). This holds for every modal
  dialog: the palette, search, settings, prompts, setup, version history,
  sign-in, sync conflicts and the rest.
- **The sidebar's edge** is a separator you can reach with Tab. **←/→**
  resize the sidebar by 16 px (**Shift**: 48 px), **Home** / **End** make it
  narrowest / widest. In right-to-left layouts the arrows follow the edge's
  direction.
- The command list in the palette can be reached with Tab and scrolled with
  the keyboard.

## Screen readers

Dialogs are announced with their names (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, a
label). The editor has a label, the palette is a combobox with a listbox,
and the sidebar edge reports its width (`aria-valuenow`).

In the editor, moving the cursor onto a heading, a task, a code fence or a
quote speaks what it is ("Heading 2: Plan", "Task, done"), in the interface
language. A new suggestion and long AI work (when it starts and when it
ends) are spoken too. From the palette:

- **Announce cursor position**: the line, the column and the heading above.
- **Screen reader announcements**: switch between headings and structure
  (the default), every line, and off.

See the [accessibility statement](/editor/accessibility-statement/) and the
[screen reader protocol](/editor/screen-reader-protocol/).

## Contrast

Text meets WCAG AA (at least 4.5:1) in light and dark mode: the accent
colour, muted text, inline code and the status-bar indicators (saved,
warning, error) were adjusted for this.

## Reduced motion

With the system's *reduce motion* setting on, animations and transitions are
cut to an instant, and scrolling that Lumen starts (the outline, comments,
typewriter mode, page view) jumps instead of gliding.

## How it is checked

- `e2e/a11y.spec.ts` runs [axe-core](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core)
  (WCAG 2.0/2.1 A and AA rules, colour contrast included) on the main
  screen, the command palette, search, the shortcuts list, theme settings and
  setup — in English (left-to-right) and Hebrew (right-to-left), light and
  dark. Any *serious* or *critical* finding fails the build.
- The same file walks a keyboard-only path: palette, a dialog that keeps
  focus for 25 Tab presses and gives it back, and the sidebar edge.
- `src/__tests__/useFocusTrap.test.tsx` covers the shared focus trap.

<!-- Generated by scripts/acr.mjs from docs/acr/wcag22.json — edit that file. -->

This report follows the structure of the VPAT® 2.5 (WCAG edition). It covers **Lumen 0.1.0** (web, desktop and mobile) against **WCAG 2.2** levels A and AA, and was last reviewed on **2026-11-10**. It is published again with every major release: `node scripts/acr.mjs --check` fails when the report's version and the app's differ.

## Summary

| Level | Supports | Partially supports | Does not support | Not applicable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 22 | 5 | 0 | 4 |
| AA | 16 | 6 | 0 | 2 |

## How it was evaluated

Automated: axe-core on six surfaces in Hebrew and English, light and dark (e2e/a11y.spec.ts); reflow at 320 and 640 px and forced colours (e2e/reflow.spec.ts); spoken announcements (e2e/sr-announce.spec.ts); unit tests of the focus trap, contrast and toasts. Manual: review of each criterion against the app's code and behaviour for this version.

## Level A

| Criterion | Status | Remarks |
|---|---|---|
| [1.1.1 Non-text Content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content) | Partially supports | Icons and icon buttons have text names (axe). Charts, diagrams, the canvas and maps drawn from note text are pictures: their alternative is the source text in the note, which is always one click away, but the picture itself has no text alternative. **Plan:** Give chart and diagram blocks a text summary (title, series, values) as their accessible name, and the canvas an outline of its shapes. (0.2.0) |
| [1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded) | Not applicable | Lumen's own interface has no prerecorded audio or video. Media in notes is the author's content. |
| [1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded) | Not applicable | No prerecorded media with sound in the interface. |
| [1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded) | Not applicable | No prerecorded video in the interface. |
| [1.3.1 Info and Relationships](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships) | Supports | Dialogs, menus, the palette (combobox + listbox), tabs, tables and forms use native elements or ARIA roles with names. In the editor, the structure of the line under the cursor (heading level, task state, code block, quote) is spoken. |
| [1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/meaningful-sequence) | Supports | The reading order follows the DOM order in both directions; Hebrew and English runs are isolated so they read in their own direction. |
| [1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/sensory-characteristics) | Supports | Instructions name the control ("the Settings button", "⌘K"), never only its shape, colour or place. |
| [1.4.1 Use of Color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color) | Partially supports | Messages, errors and selections carry text or a named icon as well as colour (axe's colour rules pass on six surfaces). In the status bar, the sync and collaboration indicators show their state by icon and colour, with the words only in a tooltip. **Plan:** Status-bar indicators with a visible word ("Synced", "Offline") and an accessible name, translated (their tooltips are English-only today). (0.2.0) |
| [1.4.2 Audio Control](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-control) | Supports | Nothing plays sound on its own. Read-aloud starts on request and has a stop control. |
| [2.1.1 Keyboard](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard) | Partially supports | Every feature is a command in the palette, dialogs keep and return focus, the sidebar edge resizes with arrow keys. The canvas whiteboard (tldraw) and the map can be panned and zoomed with the keyboard, but drawing new shapes needs a pointer. **Plan:** Keyboard commands to add, move and connect shapes on the canvas. (0.2.0) |
| [2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-keyboard-trap) | Supports | Tab in the editor indents (as in every code editor); pressing Escape and then Tab moves focus out (CodeMirror's behaviour). Dialogs release focus on Escape. |
| [2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/character-key-shortcuts) | Supports | Global shortcuts use a modifier (⌘ / Ctrl / Alt). Single-key keys work only while a component has focus (lists, the calendar grid), or in Vim mode, which is off unless turned on. |
| [2.2.1 Timing Adjustable](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/timing-adjustable) | Supports | No task has a time limit. Notifications that go away on their own stay while the pointer is over them or focus is in them (fixed for this report), and every one has a close button. |
| [2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide) | Supports | No content moves or blinks for more than five seconds, except progress spinners while work runs. With the system's reduce-motion setting, animations stop. |
| [2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold) | Supports | Nothing flashes. |
| [2.4.1 Bypass Blocks](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/bypass-blocks) | Supports | A skip link jumps to the main content; landmarks name the regions. |
| [2.4.2 Page Titled](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/page-titled) | Supports | The page title names the app ("Lumen — Markdown, illuminated"). It does not yet change with the open note: see the plan. **Plan:** Show the open note's name in the page title. (0.2.0) |
| [2.4.3 Focus Order](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-order) | Supports | Focus moves in reading order; a dialog takes focus when it opens and gives it back when it closes. |
| [2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context) | Supports | Interface links say where they go; "Learn more" links sit inside the message they belong to. |
| [2.5.1 Pointer Gestures](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-gestures) | Supports | Nothing needs a multi-point or path gesture: pinch-zoom on the canvas, the map and the graph also has buttons, the wheel or keys. |
| [2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pointer-cancellation) | Supports | Buttons act on release (native behaviour); drags can be abandoned by moving back or pressing Escape. |
| [2.5.3 Label in Name](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name) | Partially supports | Buttons with visible text use that text as their name. Not every icon-and-text control has been checked by hand. **Plan:** A manual pass over every toolbar and dialog, recorded in the screen reader protocol. (0.2.0) |
| [2.5.4 Motion Actuation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/motion-actuation) | Not applicable | No feature uses device motion. |
| [3.1.1 Language of Page](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-page) | Supports | The page's lang attribute follows the interface language (he, en, ar, …) and dir follows it. |
| [3.2.1 On Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-focus) | Supports | Focusing a control never changes the context. |
| [3.2.2 On Input](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-input) | Supports | Changing a setting applies it in place (the theme, the language); nothing navigates away or submits on input. |
| [3.2.6 Consistent Help](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help) | Supports | Help is always in the same places: ⌘/ lists the shortcuts, and the palette has Set up Lumen…, the accessibility statement, this report and Report an accessibility problem. |
| [3.3.1 Error Identification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification) | Supports | Errors are written in text next to the field, with role="alert" (for example an invalid daily-note pattern, a bad theme file, a failed sign-in). |
| [3.3.2 Labels or Instructions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions) | Supports | Every field has a visible label or an accessible name and, where needed, an example. |
| [3.3.7 Redundant Entry](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/redundant-entry) | Supports | No process asks for the same information twice; the setup wizard keeps what was entered when you go back. |
| [4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value) | Partially supports | Native controls and ARIA widgets have names, roles and states (axe, in Hebrew and English, light and dark, on six surfaces). The canvas and the map are third-party widgets with partial roles. **Plan:** Extend the axe run to every panel and dialog, and wrap the canvas and the map in labelled regions with a keyboard summary. (0.2.0) |

## Level AA

| Criterion | Status | Remarks |
|---|---|---|
| [1.2.4 Captions (Live)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-live) | Not applicable | No live audio or video in the interface (collaboration is text only). |
| [1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-prerecorded) | Not applicable | No prerecorded video in the interface. |
| [1.3.4 Orientation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/orientation) | Supports | Works in portrait and landscape; nothing locks the orientation. |
| [1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/identify-input-purpose) | Supports | Personal-data fields use autocomplete: email, current-password and new-password in sign-in. |
| [1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum) | Supports | Text is at least 4.5:1 in light and dark mode, in all built-in themes; checked by axe in Hebrew and English. |
| [1.4.4 Resize Text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/resize-text) | Supports | Text resizes to 200 % with browser zoom without loss of content or function. |
| [1.4.5 Images of Text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/images-of-text) | Supports | The interface uses real text, never pictures of text. |
| [1.4.10 Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow) | Supports | At 320 CSS px wide (400 % zoom) the main screen, side panels and dialogs fit without horizontal scrolling. Code blocks and tables scroll inside their own box (allowed for two-dimensional content). |
| [1.4.11 Non-text Contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast) | Partially supports | Focus rings, the accent and icons meet 3:1. In the default theme the borders of some text fields are lighter than 3:1 against the background; the High contrast theme meets it everywhere. **Plan:** Darken input borders (--border-strong for fields) to 3:1 in every theme, and add the check to the contrast report. (0.2.0) |
| [1.4.12 Text Spacing](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing) | Partially supports | Layouts use flexible boxes and should take the WCAG text-spacing overrides, but this has not been tested automatically yet. **Plan:** An e2e that applies the WCAG text-spacing styles to ten surfaces and checks nothing is cut off. (0.2.0) |
| [1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus) | Partially supports | Tooltips are mostly the browser's own (title). Link previews and some popovers appear on hover; not all can be dismissed with Escape without moving the pointer. **Plan:** One popover component: dismissible with Escape, hoverable, persistent until dismissed. (0.2.0) |
| [2.4.5 Multiple Ways](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/multiple-ways) | Supports | Notes can be reached from the file tree, search, the command palette (quick open), backlinks, tags and the graph. |
| [2.4.6 Headings and Labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/headings-and-labels) | Supports | Dialogs and panels have headings; fields have labels that say what they are for. |
| [2.4.7 Focus Visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible) | Supports | Every focusable element shows a focus ring, also in forced-colours mode. |
| [2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum) | Partially supports | Dialogs are modal and centred. Notifications in the corner can sit over a focused control near the bottom edge until they go away. **Plan:** Move notifications away from the focused element, and an e2e that tabs through the main screen with notifications showing. (0.2.0) |
| [2.5.7 Dragging Movements](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/dragging-movements) | Partially supports | Reordering document tabs is by dragging only; there is no single-pointer or command alternative yet. Resizing the sidebar by its edge has a keyboard alternative, but not a single-pointer one. **Plan:** "Move tab left / right" in the tab's menu and the palette, and a width menu on the sidebar edge. pages.title: Citations with [@key]
pages.description: Cite from your BibTeX, CSL-JSON or Zotero library with pandoc's [@key, p. 10], in APA, Chicago, MLA or the Israeli APA, with a reference list in the preview, DOCX and PDF.
pages.md:
## Cite in two keystrokes

Press `⌥⌘C` (or `⌘K → "Insert a citation [@key]…"`) to open the cite
dialog. It searches your whole library at once.

- With nothing typed, the sources you cited last come first: **Enter**
  cites the last one again, and **↓ Enter** the one before it.
- Type to search by author, title, year or key. Hebrew works.
- **Tab** goes to the locator field (`p. 10`, `chap. 3`, `עמ׳ 12`).
- **Enter** writes `[@key]`. **⇧Enter** writes `@key`, for a citation
  inside the sentence.

## Your library

The library is everything in the vault, read on this device:

- **BibTeX**: any `*.bib` file.
- **CSL-JSON**: `*.csl.json`, `references.json` or `bibliography.json`
  (Zotero, Zettlr and pandoc all export this format).
- **Zotero**: in the desktop app, run `⌘K → "Citations: copy the Zotero
  library into the vault"`, or press **Copy from Zotero** in the dialog.
  This copies Zotero 7's library from this computer into
  `.lumen/zotero-library.csl.json` (first turn on Settings → Advanced →
  "Allow other applications on this computer to communicate with Zotero").

Keys come from the source: the BibTeX key, CSL's `citation-key`, or a
`Citation Key:` line from Better BibTeX. Otherwise the key is the author's
family name and the year (`austen1813`, `כהן2020`).

## Pandoc syntax

| You write | APA 7 shows |
|---|---|
| `[@austen1813]` | (Austen, 1813) |
| `[@austen1813, p. 10]` | (Austen, 1813, p. 10) |
| `[see @austen1813, pp. 10–12; @darwin1859]` | (see Austen, 1813, pp. 10–12; Darwin, 1859) |
| `[-@austen1813]` | (1813) |
| `@austen1813 [p. 10] writes` | Austen (1813, p. 10) writes |

Locators can be pages, chapters, sections, figures, volumes, paragraphs,
notes or lines, in English or Hebrew. Chicago writes the page bare
(`(Austen 1813, 10)`), and so does MLA (`(Austen 10)`).

A key the library doesn't know stays as you wrote it.

## Styles

Set the style in the note's frontmatter:

```yaml
---
citation-style: il      # apa (default), chicago, mla, il
---
```

- **APA 7**, **Chicago author-date** and **MLA 9** use the 6.13 templates,
  in the note's language (Hebrew notes get ו, ואחרים, עמ׳).
- **il** is APA 7 the way Israeli academic libraries teach it:
  - Hebrew sources come first, in their own list, then the rest.
  - Each source is written in its own language.
  - Hebrew initials take a geresh: `דרשן, ד׳`.
  - The same author and year are told apart by א / ב (a / b for other
    languages).

The reference list goes where the note has pandoc's `::: {#refs}` block,
or at the end of the note. It appears in the preview, when you print to
PDF and in **Export to Word**.

All formatting is the app's own, with no citeproc and nothing fetched.

pages.title: Direction marks (bidi)
pages.description: See the invisible characters that set text direction, clean the ones that do nothing, fix reversed brackets, and catch Trojan Source text.
pages.md:
Hebrew and Arabic text pasted from a word processor, a web page or a chat
app often carries characters you cannot see. They set the direction of the
text around them, and they are the usual reason a pasted paragraph suddenly
runs the wrong way or a bracket jumps to the other end of the line. Lumen
shows them, removes the ones that do nothing, and warns you about the
dangerous ones.

## Show direction marks

Command palette (⌘K) → **Show direction marks**. Every direction control
gets a small tag in front of it, in the source editor and in WYSIWYG:

| Tag | Name | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LRM` `RLM` `ALM` | left-to-right, right-to-left, Arabic letter mark | an invisible letter of that direction; pins a line that starts with a number or a Latin word |
| `LRE` `RLE` … `PDF` | embeddings | lay out the text up to `PDF` in that direction |
| `LRO` `RLO` … `PDF` | overrides | force every character up to `PDF` into that order, even Hebrew letters |
| `LRI` `RLI` `FSI` … `PDI` | isolates | lay out a run (a URL, a name) on its own, without disturbing the line |

The character stays where it is, so the line lays out exactly as it does
anywhere else. The tag only shows you why. Run the command again to hide the
tags. The setting is kept on this device.

## Clean direction marks and fix brackets

Command palette → **Clean direction marks and fix brackets** does two things
as **one** change, so a single Undo (⌘Z) brings everything back:

- **Removes marks that change nothing on screen.** These are decided by the
  Unicode bidi algorithm (UAX #9), not guessed:
  - an `RLM` right before a Hebrew letter, or right after one;
  - an `LRM` right before or right after a Latin letter;
  - an `ALM` right after an Arabic letter;
  - an embedding or isolate with nothing inside;
  - a `PDF` or `PDI` that closes nothing.

  A mark that does change the display stays. Examples are the `RLM` in front
  of `10:30 פגישה`, an `LRM` after a number, and an `RLM` after Arabic text,
  which changes how the digits after it are read. Overrides always stay too.
- **Swaps brackets typed backwards in right-to-left lines.** `)טקסט(` was
  typed that way so it would look right in a program that did not handle
  direction. When every bracket of one kind in a line is backwards, and
  swapping them balances the line, they are swapped. Smileys (`:)`), list
  numbers (`1)`), links and left-to-right lines are left alone.

Fenced code and code spans are never changed.

## The paste warning (Trojan Source)

Two things make text display in an order other than the one it is stored in:

- an **override** (`LRO`, `RLO`);
- an embedding or isolate **left open** at the end of its line.

What you read is then not what a search, a diff or a compiler sees. This is
the "Trojan Source" attack (CVE-2021-42574).

Lumen tags these characters in **red** whether or not the marks are shown.
When you paste or drop text that contains them, a warning appears with a
**Remove them** button. The button deletes only those characters, as one
undoable change, so the text displays in the order it is stored. Harmless
isolates and marks stay.

## Limits

- **Lines are checked one at a time.** An isolate opened on one line and
  closed on the next counts as left open, as it does in the browser.
- **Only these 12 controls are covered.** Zero-width joiners and
  non-joiners are not direction controls and are not shown.

sections.heading: Clean direction marks and fix brackets
sections.text: Command palette → Clean direction marks and fix brackets does two things as one change, so a single Undo (⌘Z) brings everything back: Removes marks that change nothing on screen. These are decided by the Unicode bidi algorithm (UAX #9), not guessed: an RLM right before a Hebrew letter, or right after one; an LRM right before or right after a Latin letter; an ALM right after an Arabic letter; an embedding or isolate with nothing inside; a PDF or PDI that closes nothing. A mark that does change the display stays. Examples are the RLM in front of 10:30 פגישה, an LRM after a number, and an RLM after Arabic text, which changes how the digits after it are read. Overrides always stay too. Swaps brackets typed backwards in right-to-left lines. )טקסט( was typed that way so it would look right in a program that did not handle direction. When every bracket of one kind in a line is backwards, and swapping them balances the line, they are swapped. Smileys (:)), list numbers (1)), links and left-to-right lines are left alone. Fenced code and code spans are never changed.

sections.heading: The paste warning (Trojan Source)
sections.text: Two things make text display in an order other than the one it is stored in: an override (LRO, RLO); an embedding or isolate left open at the end of its line. What you read is then not what a search, a diff or a compiler sees. This is the "Trojan Source" attack (CVE-2021-42574). Lumen tags these characters in red whether or not the marks are shown. When you paste or drop text that contains them, a warning appears with a Remove them button. The button deletes only those characters, as one undoable change, so the text displays in the order it is stored. Harmless isolates and marks stay.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Lines are checked one at a time. An isolate opened on one line and closed on the next counts as left open, as it does in the browser. Only these 12 controls are covered. Zero-width joiners and non-joiners are not direction controls and are not shown.

pages.title: Hebrew dictionary and synonyms
pages.description: Definitions, synonyms and the niqqud of a word, from Hebrew Wiktionary, offline inside the editor.
pages.md:
Right-click a Hebrew word in the editor to see its **synonyms**, its **definition** or its
**niqqud**. Everything is looked up on this device, from a dictionary pack you download once.

## Get the dictionary

Command palette (**⌘K / Ctrl+K**) → **Hebrew dictionary and synonyms (download / remove)**.
Lumen shows the pack's size, its number of entries and its licence, and downloads it only
after you agree. The pack comes from Lumen's own site and is checked against its published
size and checksum. It is kept in the browser's storage, so it works offline. Run the same
command again to remove it.

## Use it

- **Right-click** a Hebrew word: **Synonyms**, **Definition**, **Niqqud of the word**.
  **Shift+right-click** opens the browser's own menu (copy, paste, spelling).
- Or put the cursor on the word and run **Look up the Hebrew word at the cursor**.
- Prefix letters are understood: **ובבית** finds **בית**. A synonym you click replaces the
  word and keeps its prefix (**ובבית** → **ובדירה**). The pointed form replaces the word the
  same way; the prefix letters stay unpointed.
- Text with niqqud is looked up without it.
- Synonyms go both ways: if one entry lists another word as a synonym, that word shows the
  first one too.

Nothing changes in the note until you pick a word, and then only that word, if it is
still there.

## Where the words come from

The pack is built from the **Hebrew Wiktionary** (he.wiktionary.org), whose text is licensed
**CC BY-SA 4.0**. For each entry it keeps the pointed headword, the part of speech, up to
four definitions (shortened, without examples) and the synonyms section. The credit is in
**Credits** (command palette) and in the dictionary window, and the pack ships with its
licence (`public/lexicon/LICENSE.md`).

**Why Wiktionary, not Hspell:** Hspell's word lists are AGPL-3.0, which cannot ship inside
Lumen (MIT). Lumen's spelling checker still offers Hspell as a separate download from its
upstream. Wiktionary's CC BY-SA licence applies to the pack, which is a separate file, not
to Lumen's code.

## Build the pack (maintainers)

```bash
curl -LO https://dumps.wikimedia.org/hewiktionary/latest/hewiktionary-latest-pages-articles.xml.bz2
npm run lexicon:build -- hewiktionary-latest-pages-articles.xml.bz2 20261101
```

This writes `public/lexicon/he-wiktionary.json` and `public/lexicon/manifest.json` (size,
sha256, entry count). Commit both; the app offers the download once the manifest exists.
The plan asks for at least 20,000 entries and a lookup of 20 ms or less. The lookup is a
hash lookup plus at most three prefix letters peeled; a test checks 2,000 lookups in a
25,000-entry pack, each under 20 ms.

pages.title: Hebrew grammar and style
pages.description: Hebrew grammar and style checks that run on this device, beyond spelling, with three writing levels and a short explanation for each suggestion.
pages.md:
With grammar checking on (`⌘K` → **Enable grammar check (LanguageTool)**), Hebrew
paragraphs are checked on this device. Nothing is sent anywhere. Each
suggestion comes with a one-line explanation.

## What it catches

| Error | Example | Suggestion |
|---|---|---|
| Number and gender (3–10) | שלוש ילדים | שלושה ילדים |
| Two before a noun | שתי ספרים, שניים ילדים | שני ספרים, שני ילדים |
| הכי with ביותר | הכי טוב ביותר | טוב ביותר |
| את instead of עם | נפגשתי את דני | נפגשתי עם דני |
| The article in a construct pair | הבית ספר | בית הספר |
| אני with a third-person future | אני ילך | אני אלך |
| A repeated meaning | חזר שוב, בערך כמאה | חזר, כמאה |

The rules are careful rather than greedy. If the word list cannot tell a
noun's gender, the noun is left alone, and so are compound numbers like
שלוש עשרה.

## Writing levels

`⌘K` → **Hebrew grammar: change the writing level** cycles through three
levels:

- **Everyday:** only the errors in the table above.
- **Academic** and **Legal:** also flag spoken Hebrew in formal writing, such
  as הכי חשוב (→ חשוב ביותר) and בגלל ש (→ מכיוון ש).

## A local model (optional)

The rules never need a model. If you want one, a model running in Ollama
on this computer (DictaLM 3.0 1.7B, for example) can judge each grammar
suggestion and drop the ones it rejects. The checker talks to `localhost`
only.

## How it is measured

`eval/probes/hebrew-grammar.json` has 200 sentences with one marked error
each, and the corrected sentence beside each one.
`src/__tests__/hebrewGrammar.test.ts` checks four things:
- that at least 70% of the errors are found;
- that at most 5% of the corrected sentences, and of the 1,302 sentences of
  real prose in the HeQ dev paragraphs, get any suggestion;
- the time per paragraph;
- that no request is made.

The probe was written for this repository, so its numbers are development
numbers. A held-out set of real sentences with marked errors is still
needed.

pages.title: Hebrew keyboard layout
pages.description: Shortcuts that work with the Hebrew layout on, and search that understands text typed with the wrong layout.
pages.md:
## Shortcuts work in any layout

Lumen reads a shortcut by the **key you press**, not by the letter it types.
With the Hebrew layout on, **Ctrl+K** (⌘K) still opens the palette, even
though that key types ל. The same holds for every shortcut: save, open, new,
the editor modes (⌘1–⌘4), find and replace, the shortcuts list (⌘/), undo,
redo and the rest.

With the Hebrew layout active, the shortcuts list (⌘/ / Ctrl+/) shows the
Hebrew letter on each key too: **Ctrl+K (ל)**. Lumen knows the layout from
what you last typed, or from the interface language if you haven't typed yet.

**AltGr** (Ctrl+Alt on Windows) never triggers a shortcut. Characters typed
with AltGr stay characters.

## Typed with the wrong layout

`akuo` is `שלום` typed with the English layout on, and `יקךךם` is `hello`
typed with the Hebrew one. The **command palette** and **workspace search**
read your text both ways:

- The palette shows matches for what you typed first, then matches for the
  other-layout reading, with a note: *Also showing results for “חיפוש”*.
- Search tries the other reading when what you typed finds fewer than three
  notes.

Only text in a single script is converted. Mixed Hebrew and English is taken
as you typed it.

## How it is checked

`src/__tests__/keyboardLayout.test.ts`:

- 50 golden wrong-layout queries (25 each way) must find the right command in
  the top 3, in at least 95% of cases.
- Every shortcut is checked with the English layout, the Hebrew layout and
  macOS ⌘.
- No two shortcuts may share a key, and every shortcut the palette shows must
  be the one the app binds.

`e2e/hebrew-layout.spec.ts` presses the shortcuts as the Hebrew layout sends
them.

pages.title: Hebrew and right-to-left
pages.description: How Lumen decides the direction of every block — paragraphs, tables, lists, quotes and code — in the editor, the preview, WYSIWYG and the export.
pages.md:
Lumen doesn't make a whole note right-to-left or left-to-right. Each block
reads in the direction of **its own** text, so a Hebrew paragraph sits on
the right and the English one after it on the left, in the same note.

| Block | Direction |
| --- | --- |
| Paragraph, heading | Its first strong letter (Hebrew → right-to-left) |
| List, list item, quote | Its own text: a Hebrew list has its markers and indent on the right, its quote bar on the right |
| Table (preview, export) | The table left-to-right; **each cell** by its own text |
| Table (WYSIWYG) | Each cell's paragraph by its own text |
| Code, math | Always left-to-right, even with a Hebrew comment |

The same rules apply in the source editor (line by line), the preview,
WYSIWYG and the HTML export — an exported Hebrew note opens as
`<html lang="he" dir="rtl">` with the same `dir` on every block.

## The workspace in Hebrew

With the interface in Hebrew, the whole workspace is mirrored, the way
Obsidian does it: the toolbar and the status bar start on the right, the
file tree sits on the right and the outline and backlinks on the left,
tabs run from right to left, menus open from their button's right edge,
and floating controls (the AI button, find & replace, notifications) sit
on the left. The source editor and code stay left-to-right.

The arrow keys keep their visual meaning: **←** moves to what is drawn on
the left. In the Hebrew tab strip that is the next tab; in the welcome tour
← is "next". Home and End go to the first and the last tab.

## Tested

`e2e/rtl-matrix.spec.ts` checks tables, bulleted, numbered, nested and task
lists, quotes and code in the preview, WYSIWYG and the export, with the
interface in Hebrew and in English, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and on
an iPhone 14 and a Pixel 7. `visual/rtl.visual.ts` keeps pixel baselines of
the same note (see [Visual regression](/contributing/visual-regression/)).

`e2e/rtl-parity.spec.ts` checks 20 workspace scenarios in both interface
languages and runs axe on the Hebrew workspace; `src/__tests__/rtlLogical.test.ts`
fails when app CSS, an inline style or a Tailwind class uses a physical
left / right instead of the logical start / end.

pages.title: Hebrew typography
pages.description: Gershayim, geresh, maqaf, Hebrew quotation marks and numbers, fixed as you type or for a whole note. Each rule can be turned off.
pages.md:
Word has fixed Hebrew punctuation automatically for decades. In Lumen, the
source editor does the same **as you type**, and **Hebrew typography…** in
the command palette applies it to a whole note after a preview.

| Rule | You type | You get |
|---|---|---|
| Gershayim | `צה"ל` | צה״ל |
| Geresh | `ג'ירפה` | ג׳ירפה |
| Hebrew quotation marks | `"שלום"` | „שלום” |
| Maqaf | `בית-ספר` | בית־ספר |
| Dash between words | `אחד - שניים` | אחד – שניים |
| Numbers | `50 %`, `%50`, `10–20` | 50%, 50%, 10-20 (a range reads in order right to left) |
| Mixed lines | `HTML היא שפה.` | an invisible right-to-left mark (RLM) at the start, so the line reads right to left and the period lands at its end |

Every rule works only in a Hebrew context. `say "hello"`, `it's` and `ב-2026`
stay as they are, and so does a prefix before a quote: `ו"ההגנה"` becomes
ו„ההגנה”, not a gershayim.

## Never changed

Nothing changes inside **code** (fenced blocks and inline code), **links**
and URLs, wiki-links, HTML tags, math, or the **frontmatter**.

## Undo

Each fix is its own undo step. **Ctrl+Z / ⌘Z** right after a fix gives back
the character you typed, and the next keys you type don't redo the fix. A
quotation mark right after a Hebrew letter is fixed when you type the next
key, because by then it is clear whether it is ״ (צה"ל) or a closing ”.

## Turning rules off

In **Hebrew typography…** (command palette):

- **Fix as I type** turns the automatic fixes on or off.
- Each rule has its own checkbox.
- The dialog lists every change the rules would make to the current note.
  **Apply to the note** makes them all as one undo step.

The settings are saved in this browser.

## How it is checked

`src/__tests__/hebrewTypography.test.ts` covers:

- 50 golden cases.
- A note with code, links, URLs, HTML, math and frontmatter where none of
  those change.
- Each rule turned off on its own.
- Typing character by character, including an undone fix that stays undone.

`e2e/hebrew-typography.spec.ts` types in the editor, undoes a fix, and
applies the dialog.

pages.title: Hebrew and right-to-left
pages.description: Writing in Hebrew (and Arabic) in Lumen — direction per line, the interface in Hebrew, search that ignores niqqud and prefixes, spelling on this device, and exports that keep the direction.
pages.md:
Lumen is built for notes that mix Hebrew and English.

## The interface

`⌘K → Language: …` switches the interface. Hebrew and Arabic flip the
whole layout (sidebar, menus and dialogs mirror). The interface is in 8
languages: English, Hebrew, Arabic, Russian, French, German, Japanese and
Chinese.

## Direction in a note

- **Per line, automatically.** In the source editor each line takes its
  direction from its first strong letter: a Hebrew paragraph aligns right,
  an English one left, and the cursor and selection follow. Code blocks
  and the front matter are always left-to-right.
- **For a whole note:** put `dir: rtl` (or `ltr`) in its front matter.
- **For the editor:** `⌘K → Text Direction: RTL (Right to Left)` (and back
  with *Text Direction: LTR*).

## Search

Workspace search folds niqqud, final letters (ם/מ, ן/נ…) and the prefix
letters ו ה ב כ ל מ ש, so *בבית*, *והבית* and *הַבַּיִת* all find *בית*.
The exact form ranks first. See
[Workspace search](/workspace/search/). Links between notes and heading
anchors compare names the same way, so `[[שלום]]` finds *שָׁלוֹם.md*.

## Spelling, on this device

Hebrew paragraphs are checked **locally**: a final letter inside a word, a
repeated word, a space before punctuation. For spelling against a
dictionary, download Hspell's word list once with
`⌘K → Hebrew spelling: dictionary (download / remove)` (5.7 MB). It
is AGPL-3.0, so it isn't bundled; it is stored on this device, and the
same command removes it. Turn the check on with
`⌘K → Enable grammar check (LanguageTool)`. **Hebrew text never goes to
LanguageTool**: only paragraphs that are mostly Latin are sent, with any
Hebrew words in them blanked out.

## Exports

Exports keep the direction: Word (.docx) marks Hebrew paragraphs and runs
as right-to-left, and an exported HTML file opens right-to-left when the
note is Hebrew (or its front matter says `dir: rtl`).

For the editor: ⌘K → Text Direction: RTL (Right to Left) (and back with Text Direction: LTR ).

sections.text: Workspace search folds niqqud, final letters (ם/מ, ן/נ…) and the prefix letters ו ה ב כ ל מ ש, so בבית , והבית and הַבַּיִת all find בית . The exact form ranks first. See Workspace search. Links between notes and heading anchors compare names the same way, so [[שלום]] finds שָׁלוֹם.md .

sections.heading: Spelling, on this device
sections.text: Hebrew paragraphs are checked locally : a final letter inside a word, a repeated word, a space before punctuation. For spelling against a dictionary, download Hspell's word list once with ⌘K → Hebrew spelling: dictionary (download / remove) (5.7 MB). sections.heading: Exports
sections.text: Exports keep the direction: Word (.docx) marks Hebrew paragraphs and runs as right-to-left, and an exported HTML file opens right-to-left when the note is Hebrew (or its front matter says dir: rtl).

pages.title: Legal citations (Israel)
pages.description: Rulings, laws, bills, books and articles by the Israeli uniform citation rules, and a citation from a case number in the note.
pages.md:
Lumen writes legal citations by **כללי האזכור האחיד בכתיבה המשפטית**, the third edition
(Tel Aviv University Faculty of Law, February 2021), which most Israeli law reviews and
faculties follow. Academic sources outside law use the
[Israeli APA style](/editor/citations/) ("APA 7 — Israeli academic").

## Insert a legal citation

Command palette → **Citations: legal source (uniform citation rules)…**. Choose the kind of
source, fill in the fields, and the citation is written as you type. **Insert** puts it at
the cursor, as plain text in the note, so it reads the same in the preview, in print and in
a DOCX or PDF export.

| Source | Example |
|---|---|
| Supreme Court, printed | `בג"ץ 7/48 אל-כרבוטלי נ' שר-הבטחון, פ"ד ב 5, פס' 14 (1949).` |
| Lower court, printed | `ת"פ (מקומיים י-ם) 2857/85 מדינת ישראל נ' אורנן, פ"מ התשמ"ז(ג) 334 (1987).` |
| Unpublished (Nevo) | `ת"כ (תחרות) 745-07-18 בנק מזרחי טפחות בע"מ נ' הממונה על התחרות (נבו 28.11.2019).` |
| One judge's paragraphs | `בג"ץ 8300/02 נסר נ' ממשלת ישראל, פס' 35–36 לפסק הדין של הנשיאה (בדימ') ביניש (אר"ש 22.5.2012).` |
| Law | `חוק איסור נהיגה ברכב בחוף הים, התשנ"ז–1997, ס"ח 84.` |
| A section of a Basic Law | `ס' 10 לחוק-יסוד: הממשלה, ס"ח התשס"א 158, 159.` |
| Regulations | `תקנות הנמלים (תיקון מס' 3), התשמ"א–1981, ק"ת 956.` |
| Bill | `הצעת חוק ההתיישנות, התשס"ד–2004, ה"ח הממשלה 611.` |
| Book | `אהרן ברק פרשנות במשפט כרך שני: פרשנות החקיקה (1993).` |
| Article | `יפה זילברשץ "על חופש הביטוי המסחרי" משפט וממשל ג 509, חלקים ד(3)-(4) (1996).` |

- A **printed** ruling takes its report (פ"ד, פ"מ), volume, first page and year. Leave the
  report empty for an **unpublished** one, and give the database (נבו, אר"ש) and the date.
- The **Supreme Court** has no court in parentheses; every other court does.
- A **law**: type a date (`1997-03-05`) in the year field and the Hebrew year is filled in
  (התשנ"ז). A Basic Law is cited by its collection year instead.
- **Authors** are full names, separated by commas; Hebrew joins the last one with ו
  (אהרן ברק ובני שגיא).

## From a case number in the note

Put the cursor on a case number such as `ע"א 1234/05`, `בבג״ץ 7/48` or
`ת"א (מחוזי ת"א) 12345-06-19`, and run **Citations: legal citation from the case number at
the cursor**. The picker opens with the proceeding, the court and the number filled in;
the citation you insert replaces the number. Lumen knows the common proceedings of every
court: ע"א, רע"א, דנ"א, בג"ץ, ע"פ, רע"פ, בש"פ, עע"מ, ת"א, ת"פ, ה"פ, ת"צ, ע"ע, תמ"ש and more.
Prefix letters (בע"א, ובבג"ץ) and both quote marks (" and ״) are understood.

## Checked

`src/__tests__/legalCitations.test.ts` holds 20 golden legal citations: the rules' own
examples and the same rules applied to other sources. `israeliAcademicCitations.test.ts`
holds 20 academic ones in Israeli APA. The plan asks a law student to approve at least 38 of
the 40; that review has not been done yet.
